title: Career Roadmap · CAD Operator
summary: A CAD Operator creates, edits and checks computer-aided design drawings for buildings, infrastructure, machinery and manufacturing using technical specifications and design software.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 10 for ITI drafting routes; Mathematics and technical drawing are useful.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science with Mathematics supports diploma and degree alternatives; requirements depend on the course.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Geometry, projections, dimensions, building plans and mechanical components.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Precision, spatial reasoning, computer literacy and drawing interpretation.

rows.text: Machine parts, assembly and manufacturing drawings
Survey data, site layouts and mapping
Civil CAD, construction documentation and infrastructure
Mechanical CAD, product drawings and design support

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Technical drawing, geometry, scales and dimensioning.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Core skills
blocks.text: 2D CAD, layers, blocks, layouts and drawing annotations.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: 3D modelling, drawing revisions and discipline-specific CAD or BIM tools.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Job preparation
blocks.text: Create a portfolio, check drawing accuracy and practise interpreting engineering specifications.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Residential floor plan • Mechanical component drawing • Dimensioned assembly drawing • 3D model of a simple object.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Construction, architecture, infrastructure, manufacturing, fabrication, engineering consultancy and product design.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Drawing interpretation, dimensions, projections, scale accuracy, revision control and technical documentation.

blocks.label: Tools / technologies
blocks.text: AutoCAD or equivalent CAD software, discipline-specific 3D CAD tools, BIM software for building projects, spreadsheets and PDF markup tools.
Useful credentials

items.text: DGT / NCVT Draughtsman trade certificate, where applicable.
Software-provider CAD certification relevant to the target role.
CAD / BIM training with practical portfolio work.
Advanced technical drawing or design courses.

blocks.text: Certificates are useful additions, but practical drafting ability and employer requirements remain important.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Canada, Australia, UK, Germany and New Zealand.
Institutions / routes to investigate

items.text: BCIT — Canada; building, civil or mechanical technology programs.
TAFE providers — Australia; drafting and engineering design courses.
UK further-education colleges — CAD, construction or engineering technician programs.
German universities of applied sciences — engineering and technical design programs.
New Zealand tertiary providers — construction or engineering technology programs.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic records, language proficiency where applicable, course prerequisites and portfolio evidence for some programs. Verify current course availability and international admission criteria directly with each institution.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: CAD Operator, CAD Technician, Draughtsperson, BIM Technician and Engineering Design Technician.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Construction, infrastructure, manufacturing, architecture and engineering consultancy.
